mainTopic: End of the story about מר בר רב אשי's torn ציצית and כבוד הבריות, the הדרן for פרק הקומץ, and the opening משנה of the next פרק: תכלת and לבן, and תפילין של יד and של ראש, do not hold each other back.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story about מר בר רב אשי, whose ציצית tore on שבת. In the first version, he says כבוד הבריות only pushes aside rabbinic laws (the לאו of לא תסור), so he would have thrown off the garment. In a second version (איכא דאמרי), he keeps the garment on because of כבוד הבריות. The גמרא explains that this is allowed because they were in a כרמלית, where carrying is forbidden only מדרבנן. Then פרק הקומץ ends with a הדרן. The new פרק opens with a משנה: תכלת and לבן do not hold each other back, and neither do תפילין של יד and של ראש. The גמרא asks whether this goes against רבי, who learns from ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ״ that both kinds of strings are needed together, while חכמים read it as each one alone. רב answers that the משנה can match רבי, because it is only about which string is put in first. A ברייתא backs this up: white goes before תכלת, and doing it the other way is valid but 'missing a מצוה.' The amud ends by asking what 'missing a מצוה' means.

steps.title: Human dignity only overrides the rabbinic prohibition of 'do not stray'
steps.stepSummary: The first version of the story ends: the rule of כבוד הבריות was explained as applying only to the לאו of לא תסור, meaning rabbinic laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that human dignity pushes aside a Torah prohibition was explained as talking about the prohibition of 'You shall not stray' (the Torah's command to listen to the חכמים).
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the first version of the story. The גמרא finishes its answer: רב בר שבא explained that כבוד הבריות covers only rabbinic laws. That is why מר בר רב אשי said he would have taken the garment off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'גדול כבוד הבריות' sounds like it overrides any Torah prohibition. But רב בר שבא explained that the 'Torah prohibition' meant is only לא תסור, the verse that gives rabbinic laws their force. So human dignity pushes aside rabbinic laws, not real Torah laws like carrying on שבת. That is why מר בר רב אשי said he would have thrown off the garment if he had known.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah prohibition (a 'do not' command)
'You shall not stray' (דברים 17:11), the verse behind obeying rabbinic law
Human dignity; not embarrassing a person in public

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think כבוד הבריות can override any Torah law. Here it is limited to rabbinic laws, which get their power from the לאו of לא תסור.

phrases.english: With regard to the prohibition of "You shall not stray."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:11. This finishes a sentence that started before this section, where רב בר שבא explained the rule this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from before this section: the כבוד הבריות rule is limited to rabbinic law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כבוד הבריות overrides any Torah prohibition, even carrying on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: כבוד הבריות overrides only rabbinic prohibitions (the לאו of לא תסור).

steps.title: Second version: told right away, he refuses to remove the garment
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, רבינא told מר בר רב אשי about the tear right there. מר בר רב אשי refused to throw off the garment and cited גדול כבוד הבריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell the story differently: רבינא told him while they were still out there. מר בר רב אשי answered: What are you thinking, that I should throw it off? Didn't the Master say, 'Great is human dignity, for it pushes aside a Torah prohibition'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second version of the same story. Here מר בר רב אשי heard about the tear in the street and decided to keep wearing the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, he would have taken the garment off. In this version, he relies on כבוד הבריות and keeps it on, even though wearing invalid ציצית outside on שבת looks like carrying. This sets up the next question: how can he use that rule if it only overrides rabbinic laws?

keyTerms.meaning: To throw it off
Pushes aside, overrides
A negative commandment

phrases.english: And there are those who say
he told him right from there,
phrases.notes: Meaning רבינא told him about the tear while they were still out in the street, not after they got home.

phrases.english: and he said to him: What is your thinking, that I should throw it off?
But didn't the Master say: Great is human dignity,
for it pushes aside a prohibition in the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same story, where the outcome is the opposite.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בר רב אשי kept the garment on, relying on the rule that כבוד הבריות overrides a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: Challenge: the rule was limited to rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רב בר שבא explained that כבוד הבריות only overrides the לאו of לא תסור, so how could it allow carrying on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב בר שבא explained this rule in front of רב כהנא as referring only to the prohibition of 'You shall not stray'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. It reminds us that the rule only covers rabbinic laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in a public domain on שבת is a real Torah prohibition. If כבוד הבריות only overrides rabbinic laws, it should not let מר בר רב אשי keep wearing the garment. So his reasoning seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, interpreted it
In front of him

phrases.english: But Rav bar Shaba explained it
in front of Rav Kahana
as referring to the prohibition of "You shall not stray,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּרְגְּומַהּ רַב בַּר שְׁבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר בר רב אשי's reliance on כבוד הבריות in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's decision to keep wearing the garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כבוד הבריות only overrides rabbinic laws, but carrying on שבת is a Torah law.

steps.title: Answer: the place was a כרמלית, which is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The place where they were walking was a כרמלית, where carrying is forbidden only מדרבנן, so כבוד הבריות can override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the place was a כרמלית, which is only a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends the second version of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית is an in-between area, not a full public domain. By Torah law you may carry there, and the ban is only rabbinic. So keeping the garment on there broke only a rabbinic law, and כבוד הבריות may override that.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between area, neither fully private nor fully public, where carrying on שבת is forbidden only rabbinically
Of the חכמים, rabbinic law
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: כבוד הבריות overrides rabbinic prohibitions, including carrying in a כרמלית, but not real Torah prohibitions.

phrases.english: Here too,
it was a karmelit, which is forbidden by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by explaining what kind of place it was.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He was in a full public domain, where carrying is a Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was in a כרמלית, where carrying is only rabbinic, so כבוד הבריות applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the halacha that human dignity can push aside rabbinic laws.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הקומץ
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the chapter הקומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הקומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter is over. This line says goodbye to it and promises to come back and learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is taught here. It is the traditional way of closing a פרק, and the next line starts a new chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula for finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaKometz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that contained the discussion above.

steps.title: משנה: the ציצית colors and the two תפילין don't hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה teaches that תכלת and לבן in ציצית do not hold each other back, and neither do תפילין של יד and של ראש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Not having the blue (תכלת) strings does not stop you from doing the מצוה with the white ones, and not having the white does not stop you from doing it with the blue. Not having the arm תפילין does not stop you from putting on the head ones, and not having the head ones does not stop you from putting on the arm ones.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It teaches that each part of these two מצוות can be done on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'מעכב' means 'holds back': one missing part makes the other useless. The משנה says this is not so here. If you have only white strings you still wear them, and if you have only one of the תפילין you still put it on. The גמרא will next ask whether this agrees with רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The sky-blue dyed strings of ציצית
The white strings of ציצית
Holds back; makes the מצוה invalid without it
The תפילין worn on the arm
The תפילין worn on the head

steps.confusionAlert: 'Does not hold back' does not mean you only need one. Ideally you do both. It means that if one is missing, you still do the other.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַתְּכֵלֶת אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת הַלָּבָן,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: The blue does not hold back the white,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if you don't have the blue strings, you can still do the מצוה with the white ones.

phrases.english: and the white does not hold back the blue.

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל יָד אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: The arm tefillin does not hold back the head one,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל רֹאשׁ אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת שֶׁל יָד.
phrases.english: and the head one does not hold back the arm one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַתְּכֵלֶת אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת הַלָּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter, unrelated to the story above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תכלת and לבן do not hold each other back, and תפילין של יד and של ראש do not hold each other back; each may be done alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for wearing ציצית without תכלת today, and for putting on one of the תפילין when the other is not available.

steps.title: Is the משנה against רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי, who holds from ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ״ that תכלת and לבן hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי? A ברייתא teaches: ״And you shall see it,″ which teaches that they hold each other back. These are the words of רבי. חכמים say: they do not hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the discussion of the new משנה. It suggests the משנה matches only חכמים and goes against רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said תכלת and לבן are not מעכב each other. A ברייתא shows that רבי disagrees and holds they are מעכב each other. So it looks like the משנה follows חכמים and not רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that may later be pushed away.
Hold each other back. Without one, the other does not count.
"And you shall see it." The פסוק about ציצית that רבי learns from.
The Sages who disagree with רבי.

steps.confusionAlert: Here "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: גמרא:
Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי?
For it was taught: "And you shall see it" —
this teaches that they hold each other back,
phrases.notes: "They" means the תכלת strings and the white strings.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי;
and the חכמים say: they do not hold each other back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose view the משנה from step 6 follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that תכלת and לבן are not מעכב each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי holds they are מעכב, so the משנה seems to go against רבי.

steps.title: What is רבי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי learns from the פסוק that the two kinds of strings hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask how רבי gets his view from the פסוק. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ״ do not obviously mention two kinds of strings. So the גמרא asks how רבי learns from them that both are needed together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? It asks for the source or logic behind a view.

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי's view quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי learns from ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ״ that תכלת and לבן are מעכב each other.

steps.title: רבי reads "it" as both strings together
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק mentions strings like the corner, meaning white, and a thread of תכלת. Then it says "see it" in the singular, so both must be there as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written "the corner," meaning strings of the same kind as the corner, and it is written "a thread of תכלת." Then the Torah says "and you shall see it," meaning only when both are there together as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's source. One פסוק lists two kinds of strings, and the next פסוק calls them "it," as one thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The corner" points to strings the same kind as the garment's corner, which are usually white. Since the Torah calls both kinds together "it," in the singular, רבי learns they make up one מצוה. So each one alone does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The same kind as the corner, meaning white strings like the garment.
A thread of sky-blue wool.
The Merciful One. A name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah.
Both of them together as one.

phrases.english: As it is written: "the corner" — the same kind as the corner,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38. Garments were usually white, so this means white strings.

phrases.english: and it is written: "a thread of תכלת,"
and the Merciful One says: "and you shall see it" —
not until both of them are there together as one.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular word "it," said about both white and תכלת, shows they form one מצוה. So both are needed.

steps.title: חכמים read "it" as each string on its own
steps.stepSummary: חכמים read ״וּרְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ״ as meaning that each kind of string counts on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? "And you shall see it" means each one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן handle the same פסוק. They read "it" as referring to each kind of string separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same word, "it." רבי says "it" joins the two strings into one unit. The רבנן say "it" refers to each kind alone, so one kind without the other still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Each one by itself.
Means; it implies.

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: how do the רבנן explain this same פסוק?

phrases.english: "And you shall see it" —
means each one by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's reading of the same פסוק that רבי used in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "It" refers to each kind of string individually, so they are not מעכב each other.

steps.title: Back to the question: is the משנה against רבי?
steps.stepSummary: After explaining both views, the גמרא returns to its question: shall we say the משנה goes against רבי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה is not like רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its opening suggestion now that both readings are clear. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we understand why רבי says the strings are מעכב. So the problem returns: the משנה says they are not מעכב, which seems to go against him.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is not like רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the suggestion of step 7 after the side discussion in steps 8 through 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the strings are not מעכב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי clearly holds they are מעכב, so the משנה seems to go against him.

steps.title: The משנה can match רבי: it is about which comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the משנה can even match רבי. It only teaches about the order in which the strings are put in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: You can even say the משנה follows רבי. It is needed only to teach about putting one before the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not have to argue with רבי. Its "not מעכב" rule is about the order of the strings, not about having both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer reads the משנה in a new way. Even רבי agrees that both strings are needed. The משנה only teaches that if they were put in the wrong order, the מצוה still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. It shows the view can fit even the opinion we thought it went against.
It is needed only for. It narrows what a teaching is really about.
To put first; which comes before the other.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי and חכמים argue whether תכלת and לבן are needed together. According to רב, the משנה fits even רבי, because "not מעכב" refers only to the order of putting them in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns the משנה from a debate about needing both strings into a rule about order. It leads into the next ברייתא about white coming before תכלת.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
You can even say it follows רבי,
it is needed only for which comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי, לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְקַדֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 11 by reading the משנה in a narrower way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the משנה's case so it no longer argues with רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's "not מעכב" meant that one kind of string works without the other at all, which goes against רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only teaches that the wrong order does not ruin the מצוה, which even רבי accepts.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows there is a set order for the strings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the white should be put in before the תכלת. If someone did it the other way, he is still יוצא but has missed a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The מצוה is to put the white before the תכלת. If he put the תכלת before the white, he is יוצא, but he has missed a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב's answer that the משנה is only talking about the order in which the strings are put in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the משנה is about order, not about one string holding back the other. This ברייתא shows that an order really exists: white first, then תכלת. Doing it the wrong way does not ruin the ציצית, since he is still יוצא. It is only a missed piece of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To put first, to do before
He has fulfilled his obligation
He is missing (part of) a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Missed a מצוה' does not mean the ציצית are not valid. The ברייתא clearly says he is יוצא. It means he did not do the מצוה in the best way.

phrases.english: As it is taught: It is a מצוה to put the white before the sky-blue,
and if he put the sky-blue before the white, he has fulfilled his obligation,
except that he has missed a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's answer in Step 12 by showing a ברייתא that sets an order for the strings.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the משנה teaches only the order for putting in the strings, so it can match רבי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the מצוה is white before תכלת, and doing it the other way is valid but missing a מצוה.

steps.title: What does 'missed a מצוה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means when it says he 'missed a מצוה,' since it also says he is יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he missed a מצוה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the words 'missed a מצוה' in the ברייתא. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says two things that seem to pull apart: he is יוצא, yet he 'missed a מצוה.' The גמרא wants to know what exactly is missing if the ציצית still count.

keyTerms.meaning: What, what does it mean

phrases.english: What does it mean that he missed a מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of a phrase from the ברייתא quoted in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is missing when someone puts the תכלת in first, if he is still יוצא.
